article.headline: Google Brings No-Code Agent Orchestration to the Enterprise
article.lede: At Cloud Next on April 22, 2026, Google unveiled the Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform, with **Agent Designer** as its centerpiece — a drag-and-drop canvas that lets business users wire together AI agents without writing a line of code. The pitch is familiar from the robotic-process-automation wave of the 2010s, but the underlying substrate has changed considerably.
article.body:
Gemini Enterprise is itself a rebrand: Google called the product *AgentSpace* until late 2024, when it folded the service into the broader Gemini umbrella. Agent Designer sits inside that platform as a no-code *orchestration layer* — meaning its job is not to run a single AI model but to sequence, route between, and supervise multiple specialized agents. The drag-and-drop interface exposes nodes for triggers, data connectors, and individual agents, which users connect visually rather than through configuration files or API calls.

The agent gallery Google ships out of the box includes recognizable branded tools — Deep Research, NotebookLM, and an Idea Generation agent described as a "competitive, multi-agent tournament" that pits candidate solutions against each other before surfacing a winner. Organizations can also define custom agents that reach into internal systems: the image accompanying the post shows examples tapping BigQuery sales data, scraping competitor TikTok and Pinterest feeds for trend signals, and routing tasks across team communication channels.

The competitive frame matters. Microsoft's *Copilot Studio*, Salesforce's *Einstein* platform, and AWS's *Bedrock AgentCore* are all targeting the same buyer: the enterprise IT department that wants AI automation without a team of ML engineers. Google's differentiator, at least on paper, is native integration with its own data stack — BigQuery, Google Drive, and Google Workspace — which many large organizations already run. Whether that integration depth proves decisive or merely table-stakes will depend on how quickly the other platforms close the gap.

For builders who outgrow the no-code canvas, Google offers a code-first path through the *Agent Development Kit* (ADK) and deployment via Vertex AI Agent Builder. The two surfaces share the same runtime, so an agent prototyped in Agent Designer can, in principle, be handed off to an engineering team for extension — a design choice that distinguishes it from earlier no-code tools that created hard handoff cliffs.

concepts.definition: The practice of coordinating multiple AI agents so they hand tasks to one another in a defined sequence or in parallel, with one agent's output becoming another's input. Orchestration handles routing logic, error recovery, and result aggregation that a single model could not manage alone.

A visual development environment where users assemble software behavior by connecting graphical components rather than writing source code. No-code tools lower the barrier to building automations but typically impose limits on customization compared with hand-written code.

An AI architecture in which several specialized models or agents operate concurrently or in sequence, each handling a subtask it is optimized for. The Idea Generation agent described here is one example: it runs multiple agents in competition before producing a consolidated answer.

ticker_googl.name: Alphabet Inc. (Class A)
ticker_googl.blurb: Alphabet is the parent company of Google, the world's dominant search engine, as well as YouTube, the Google Cloud Platform, and a portfolio of moonshot bets (Waymo, DeepMind, Verily). Search advertising accounts for the majority of revenue, but the cloud division has grown into a multi-billion-dollar profit centre. Alphabet is also a leading player in generative AI, having developed the Gemini family of large language models and integrated them across its product suite.
ticker_googl.recent: Alphabet reported FY2025 revenue of approximately $370 billion, with Google Cloud crossing $50 billion annually. The company has faced antitrust scrutiny in both the US and EU, with a US federal court ruling in 2024 that Google holds an illegal monopoly in general search. Despite regulatory headwinds, the stock has benefited from AI-driven search enhancements and strong cloud growth. Paul Pelosi exercised call options with a $150 strike (purchased January 2025, exercised January 2026) gaining approximately 75% over the period.

sources.title: Nancy Pelosi's 2026 Stock Moves — Motley Fool

ticker_msft.name: Microsoft Corporation
ticker_msft.description: Microsoft is a global software, cloud, and AI platform company. Its principal segments are Productivity and Business Processes (Office, LinkedIn, Dynamics), Intelligent Cloud (Azure, server products), and More Personal Computing (Windows, Xbox, Surface). The company is in a structural transition from a capital-light software licensor to a capital-intensive hyperscale cloud and AI infrastructure provider.
